top_choice_rationale: Magic-wavelength trapping is a distinct physical idea (the trap shifts both clock levels equally) that lets many atoms be interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, and the resulting 10^-18 performance has been reproduced and cross-compared by independent laboratories (RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE). Katori (proposal and first Sr lattice clock) and Ye (long coherence, systematic evaluation, 10^-18 accuracy, many-body operation) hold two different kinds of original, decisive work, and the citation naming magic-wavelength trapping separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-trap prizes. Residual concerns (Ye's separate credit, claims of Lemonde, Lisdat, Takamoto and others, prospective fundamental-physics reach) do not outweigh the maturity of the result, so an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Katori or Ye; long-time collaborator of 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier and adjacent to atomic metrology, but no recorded tie to any credited name on P001
